- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot after spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.30) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays mean reversion, especially after strong sentiment shifts.
- Avoid overreacting to recent sentiment swings — model overweights sentiment in short-term forecasts.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates volatility in high-sentiment periods — adjust upward by 2–5% when sentiment > 0.15.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.00–0.10), model tends to underestimate — add 1–3% to forecast.
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in 30-day forecasts — apply a 3–5% upward bias to peak values.
- If sentiment is rising and price is trending up, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.
